question: Why did one of America's best-known film actresses of 1909 appear on no poster by name?
answer: Her studio did not name its players. Florence Lawrence was billed as the Biograph Girl until Carl Laemmle's IMP company hired her; in March 1910 it advertised, under the headline We Nail a Lie, that rumours of her death were false. Whether Laemmle began the rumour is disputed. The denial made her a name.
move: Whoever controls the credit decides who becomes known.
ask: Whose name gets credit for work that many hands did, and who decides?
reference: Richard deCordova, Picture Personalities: The Emergence of the Star System in America, University of Illinois Press, 1990
